nodes.label:
Laptop Flagged
for Retirement
nodes.title: Laptop Flagged for Retirement
nodes.info: Arrives either from Chapter 22's repair workflow, as damage beyond basic repair, or simply from reaching the end of its expected service life.

nodes.label:
Still
Functional?
nodes.title: Still Functional?
nodes.info: A working-but-outdated laptop has more options than a laptop that no longer powers on or holds a charge.

nodes.label:
Evaluate for
Donation
nodes.title: Device Donation Program
nodes.info: The club's practice of accepting still-functional donated laptops from companies, families, or other organisations, and of donating its own retired-but-working devices onward instead of discarding them -- a two-way flow.

nodes.label:
Another Program
Can Use It?
nodes.title: Another Program Can Use It?
nodes.info: Some still-working laptops fit another club or family's needs even after this club retires them.

nodes.label: Donated Outward
nodes.title: Donated Outward
nodes.info: Data is wiped per the device security policy, then the laptop is donated to another program through the club's donation program.

nodes.label:
Device End-of-Life
Plan
nodes.title: Device End-of-Life Plan
nodes.info: The club's written procedure for a laptop no longer safe, repairable, or worth updating: wipe all student data first, per the device security policy, then recycle it through a certified recycler.

nodes.label:
Refurbished Device
Sourcing
nodes.title: Refurbished Device Sourcing
nodes.info: Deliberately buying previously used, professionally reconditioned laptops instead of new ones -- trading a shorter expected lifespan and warranty for a substantially lower price. The other end of the same flow: one club's retirement is another's intake.

legend.text: The same flow, seen from the receiving club
